impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The Career Development Plan (D1.3, WP1), agreed by M3 and reviewed at the five steering points M6/M12/M16/M20/M27, together with the non-academic placement at AgroVIR (WP5, tasks T5.4 and T5.6), operationalises the fellow's transition from a plant-physiology background into the researcher profile OC6 describes — one combining biological understanding, scalable geospatial prediction and operational decision support. This directly improves employability and career mobility within academia and beyond. Explicit Tier 3 linkage: impacts.json EI-01 -> D1.3; outcomes.json OC6 produced_by D1.3.
impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: expected_impacts.json EI-01; source_section 'Expected Outcome — For supported postdoctoral fellows'; HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01-01.slice.json

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Strengthened international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary collaboration is evidenced along three concrete project axes: the Hungary->Bulgaria zero-shot and calibrated transfer test executed with MVCRI (WP4 tasks T4.3-T4.5, deliverable D4.2, outcome OC3) supplies the international axis; the AgroVIR functional/technical evaluation and farmer-field placement (WP5 tasks T5.4/T5.6, deliverable D5.4, outcome OC4) supply the inter-sectoral axis; and the two-way exchange between plant physiology and geoinformatics realised across WP2-WP3 supplies the interdisciplinary axis. Explicit Tier 3 linkage: impacts.json EI-02 -> D4.2, D5.4.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Alignment of researcher working conditions with the European Charter for Researchers is evidenced at instrument level by the Career Development Plan (D1.3, WP1), supported by ELTE open recruitment and researcher-development policies and by the supervision and training arrangements. This contributes to a more equitable and attractive European research environment, carried by the reviewed CDP underpinning outcome OC6. Tier 3 records this as the thinnest of the six mappings (no external accreditation; the HRS4R claim was permanently removed per C8). Explicit Tier 3 linkage: impacts.json EI-04 -> D1.3.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Increased R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer is delivered through three reusable project outputs: the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library (D2.2, WP2, outcome OC1), the released FIELDWISE predictive engine with its published model card (D3.2, WP3, outcome OC2) and the adaptation protocol (D4.3, WP4, outcome OC3). Together with the §1.3 two-way transfer between the fellow and ELTE and the partner contributions of MATE, MVCRI and AgroVIR, these constitute concrete knowledge-transfer instruments that raise R&I capacity across participating organisations. Explicit Tier 3 linkage: impacts.json EI-05 -> D2.2, D3.2, D4.3.

kpis.description: Career Development Plan agreed and reviewed across the fellowship's steering points, evidencing the OC6 career profile transition.
kpis.target: CDP agreed by M3 and reviewed at all five steering points (M6, M12, M16, M20, M27).
kpis.measurement_method: Verification of the signed CDP at M3 and dated review minutes at each of the five steering points.

kpis.description: Cross-country Hungary->Bulgaria transfer gap quantified via the MVCRI collaboration (international collaboration axis).
kpis.target: Zero-shot and locally calibrated Hungary-to-Bulgaria performance both reported.
kpis.measurement_method: Inspection of the Hungary->Bulgaria transferability report for both reported performance regimes, reported to Prof. Vinelina Yankova at MVCRI.

kpis.description: External inter-sectoral evaluation completed by AgroVIR (inter-sectoral collaboration axis).
kpis.target: The AgroVIR report covers all nine assessment dimensions listed in §1.2.
kpis.measurement_method: Checklist verification that the AgroVIR functional/technical evaluation addresses each of the nine assessment dimensions.

kpis.description: Charter-aligned working conditions evidenced at instrument level through the agreed and reviewed Career Development Plan.
kpis.target: CDP agreed by M3 and reviewed at all five steering points, with supervision and training arrangements documented under ELTE researcher-development policy.
kpis.measurement_method: Verification of the signed CDP and its five dated reviews against the European Charter for Researchers principles and ELTE recruitment/development policy references.
kpis.source_ref: impacts.json KPI K11 (D1.3); impacts.json EI-04 mapping; outcomes.json OC6

kpis.description: Sentinel-2 transferability of hyperspectral features verdicted in the transfer library (knowledge-transfer output).
kpis.target: Every candidate hyperspectral feature carries an explicit transferable or hyperspectral-only verdict.
kpis.measurement_method: Audit of the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library for a recorded verdict against each candidate feature.

kpis.description: Released predictive engine documented via a published model card (reusable R&I output).
kpis.target: One model card published for the released predictive engine.
kpis.measurement_method: Confirmation of a published model card accompanying the released FIELDWISE predictive engine.

kpis.description: Local-calibration adaptation cost stated in the adaptation protocol (knowledge-transfer output).
kpis.target: The adaptation protocol states the minimum local calibration volume needed.
kpis.measurement_method: Inspection of the adaptation protocol for an explicit statement of the minimum local calibration volume.

activities.activity_type: Peer-reviewed open-access publication of the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel-2 transferability findings and the methodological bridge between proximal hyperspectral observation and scalable Sentinel-based prediction (IMP-SCI)
activities.target_audience: Agricultural remote-sensing and geoinformatics researchers, and plant-physiology / crop-stress modelling scientists working on transferable agricultural AI
activities.timing: Submissions from the mid-fellowship steering point onward (M12-M27), aligned with release of D2.2 and D3.2

activities.activity_type: Public release of the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library (D2.2) with recorded per-feature transferability verdicts, for reuse by the research community
activities.target_audience: Earth-observation and agricultural-AI research groups reusing feature-transfer methods

activities.activity_type: Release of the FIELDWISE predictive engine with its published model card (D3.2) and the local-calibration adaptation protocol (D4.3) to research organisations
activities.target_audience: Research organisations and modelling teams adapting the engine to new regions (knowledge-transfer recipients incl. MATE, MVCRI)
activities.timing: At D3.2 and D4.3 delivery (WP3, WP4)

activities.activity_type: Delivery of the Hungary-to-Bulgaria zero-shot and calibrated transferability report (D4.2) to the international collaboration partner
activities.target_audience: MVCRI research staff (Prof. Vinelina Yankova) and the wider cross-country agricultural-AI transfer community

dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All peer-reviewed publications arising from the fellowship are made available in open access, and the released model card (D3.2), transfer library (D2.2) and adaptation protocol (D4.3) are published as open, reusable research outputs. Research data is managed under a Data Management Plan delivered within the first six months and curated to be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR), consistent with MSCA open-science practice.

activities.activity_type: Advancement of FIELDWISE from a desktop research prototype to a scientifically validated web MVP (D5.1) serving stress probability, uncertainty, spatial risk, irrigation priority and temporal evolution (IMP-TECH)
activities.expected_result: A reachable, operational decision-support MVP whose outputs support irrigation timing and spatial prioritisation decisions

activities.activity_type: External functional/technical evaluation of the MVP against real agricultural-software requirements by the non-academic partner (D5.4), covering all nine assessment dimensions
activities.expected_result: Evidence on operational fitness and uptake readiness from an end-user perspective, informing further exploitation
activities.timing: During the AgroVIR placement (WP5, tasks T5.4/T5.6)

activities.activity_type: Definition of an FMIS integration roadmap (D5.5) naming required interfaces and post-fellowship steps for embedding the engine in farm-management information systems
activities.expected_result: A documented path to integrate FIELDWISE into operational agricultural software beyond the fellowship

activities.activity_type: Use of the local-calibration adaptation protocol (D4.3) to enable transfer of the trained models to new growing regions
activities.expected_result: Reduced adaptation cost stated as the minimum local calibration volume, supporting reuse in other European environments (IMP-EU)

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: Tier 3 records no explicit IP protection data for the fellowship. The default exploitation posture is open: the predictive engine is released with a published model card (D3.2) and the transfer library (D2.2) and adaptation protocol (D4.3) are published as reusable outputs, so exploitation proceeds primarily through open release and non-academic uptake rather than formal protection. Any protectable outcome identified during the AgroVIR evaluation and FMIS roadmap work (D5.4/D5.5) would be assessed jointly by the host and partner before disclosure; no patent or other formal protection is presently claimed.

sustainability_mechanism.description: Results persist beyond the fellowship through several durable, project-grounded channels: the released FIELDWISE predictive engine with its published model card (D3.2) and the FMIS integration roadmap (D5.5) provide a maintained, integrable software asset and a concrete post-fellowship uptake path validated by AgroVIR; the open transfer library (D2.2) and local-calibration adaptation protocol (D4.3) let other European regions reuse and re-calibrate the methods at a stated minimum calibration cost, sustaining the cross-country transferability contribution (IMP-EU); and integration of the research results into ELTE teaching — co-design and delivery of a full module unit within an ELTE MSc course on Earth observation for agriculture (EI-06) — carries the knowledge forward into education. The reviewed Career Development Plan (D1.3) sustains the fellow's own capacity to continue the line of work after the fellowship.

activities.activity_type: Public field demonstration of the FIELDWISE decision-support tool for growers
activities.target_audience: Processing-tomato growers and farm operators in the AgroVIR farmer network (growers as a public audience, not researchers)
activities.objective: Broaden public engagement with the research by showing, in-field, how the tool supports irrigation timing and stress detection, and gather grower feedback

activities.activity_type: Public-facing article for a general and sector audience, published annually
activities.target_audience: The interested public and regional / agricultural-sector press readership
activities.objective: Communicate the aims and results of the fellowship in accessible language and raise public understanding of transferable agricultural AI for water-efficient farming
activities.timing: One article per year across the fellowship duration
